title: Ask For
The Favour

post.title: Want Someone to Like You? Ask Them for a Favour #shorts
post.description: Would you dare ask? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who never asks anyone for anything. Arthur needs a favour from Otto, his grumpy boss, and he'd rather struggle alone than ask. Benjamin Franklin wrote in his autobiography that he won over a rival legislator by asking to borrow a rare book; the man was friendlier from then on. In 1969, Jon Jecker and David Landy tested the idea ('Liking a Person as a Function of Doing Him a Favour', Human Relations): after a study where people won money, the researcher personally asked some of them to give it back because he was paying out of his own pocket. Those he asked liked him more than those who weren't asked, or who were asked by a secretary on behalf of the department. One common explanation is cognitive dissonance: 'I helped him, so I must like him.' It was a small study, so treat it as a nudge, not a guarantee, and keep the ask small. #psychology #shorts #benfranklineffect #socialskills #overthinking
